practice_note: Optional and ungraded. Choose one activity for about 10 minutes within your existing practice time. Stop after the stated check if it answers your question; you do not need to finish every stage or earn a completion badge. No upload, screenshot, extra model run or D2L submission is required. D2L remains authoritative for graded work.

weeks.title: Foundations and prediction
weeks.intro: Choose one activity to connect a weighted sum or output choice with this week’s prediction notebook.

activities.title: Neuron Explorer
activities.focus: Trace a weighted sum and ReLU. Change one weight and explain its effect on the output.
activities.transfer: Connect the result to one forward pass in the HAR notebook.

activities.title: Sigmoid vs Softmax
activities.focus: Compare independent outputs with mutually exclusive classes. Explain why HAR uses a competing class distribution.
activities.transfer: Use the comparison to explain your output-layer choice; this is practice, not a D2L quiz.

weeks.title: Backpropagation and optimization
weeks.intro: Choose one activity before checking your implementation or training update.

activities.title: Backprop Table
activities.focus: Follow one chain of local derivatives and explain the sign of the input gradient.
activities.transfer: Compare the reasoning with your Assignment 1 finite-difference check.

activities.title: Momentum SGD
activities.focus: Compare one supplied SGD update with a momentum update. Explain what the velocity remembers.
activities.transfer: The supplied gradients illustrate update arithmetic; they are not a benchmark of optimizer quality.

weeks.title: Regularization and validation
weeks.intro: Choose one activity to explain your existing baseline/regularization comparison.

activities.title: Regularization Race
activities.focus: Compare the effect of L1 and L2 on one weight and its update.
activities.transfer: Connect one change to the regularization mechanism in Assignment 2; do not add a new required model run.

activities.title: Early Stopping
activities.focus: Move the stopping epoch and distinguish choosing a checkpoint from fitting its parameters.
activities.transfer: The 1,000-example split is a toy exercise. Keep the course’s fixed participant-separated HAR split; do not re-split it.

weeks.title: Convolutional networks
weeks.intro: Choose one activity to explain a convolution or a pooling output shape.

activities.title: Convolution
activities.focus: Work through one filter position and predict the next output.
activities.transfer: The example is two-dimensional; relate the same shared-filter idea to the one-dimensional HAR signal candidate.

activities.title: Adaptive Pooling
activities.focus: Change the input length and compare fixed-window pooling with a fixed output size.
activities.transfer: Explain what remains fixed before the dense classifier. This is optional architecture practice.

weeks.title: Recurrence and attention
weeks.intro: Choose one activity to explain where sequence order enters a model.

activities.title: RNN Forward
activities.focus: Trace one recurrent update, then compare the same inputs in a different order.
activities.transfer: Relate the hidden-state trace to time-ordered HAR windows.

activities.title: Transformer Positional Encoding
activities.focus: Compare reordered tokens with and without position information.
activities.transfer: Use the permutation comparison to explain why a signal-attention candidate needs time-position information.

weeks.title: Evaluation and interpretation
weeks.intro: Choose one activity to support an error analysis you already need for the project.

activities.title: Choosing the Right Metric
activities.focus: Compare accuracy and recall as the decision threshold changes.
activities.transfer: All clinical counts are a teaching scenario, not clinical evidence. Transfer the metric trade-off to a HAR confusion matrix.

activities.title: Gradient Attribution
activities.focus: Compare a gradient with a feature-removal effect in one supplied toy example.
activities.transfer: Explain why an attribution score depends on the method and reference. It is not proof of a causal explanation.

weeks.title: Experiment synthesis
weeks.intro: Reuse your existing curves and results; no new training run is needed.

activities.title: Learning Curves
activities.focus: Use a training/validation pattern to distinguish poor fit from a generalization gap.
activities.transfer: Apply one diagnosis to your baseline/candidate comparison and state a limitation. Do not collect new data or exceed the project run budget.
